drafted_from: tool:render-an-edit's own row in tools/media-composition/tool-rows.json, tools/media-composition/do-work/render-an-edit.mjs, and the script run on a synthetic 7 second clip
start_here: Say to your AI: "Render an edit of my video: its first 2 seconds, then 4 to 6.5 seconds at double speed." It runs tool:render-an-edit with that edit and saves the video in your files.
no_lists_because: It makes a new video in your files from the video you name and keeps no list of its own.
instructions: 1. Find your clip's identity and exact length in bytes in your files; it goes in files as {name: "source.mp4", identity, bytes}.

2. Write the edit as JSON: spine.segments is a list of clips ({kind: "clip", id, source: the clip's identity, in, out, speed}), optionally encode {width, height}, subtitles.ass and audio_graph.music_bed. Any source is a file identity from your files.

3. Say "Render this edit" and the AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run and tool tool:render-an-edit with files and edl. The door runs it in a container and answers {"result": {...}}; an error comes back as {"error": "what to change"}.
4. Read result (duration_seconds, width, height, has_audio, bytes, segments) and files.video, the rendered video in your files.

worked_examples.title: Two clips, the second at double speed
worked_examples.ask: Render the first 2 seconds, then 4 to 6.5 seconds at double speed.
worked_examples.given: read from tools/media-composition/do-work/render-an-edit.mjs and run on a 7 second 320x180 clip: 2 seconds, then 2.5 seconds at double speed (1.25 s) is about 3.25 seconds in 2 segments; with no encode size the edit keeps the first clip's own size
